race: Formula 1 Gran Premio de la Ciudad de México 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to the Race Weekend Podcast, and Mexico City is the stage for a title that could be settled in front of a roaring, passionate crowd, with the whole paddock watching.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: We are deep into the season, and this is not just another Grand Prix, this is the moment Antonelli could become champion, and the atmosphere will be electric.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The data points the same way, but there is still plenty of drama to chase, plus a track that loves strong drivers, and every lap matters.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The big news is Kimi is missing Thursday media day with an illness, but that is only media day, not the race weekend.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He just won the United States Grand Prix, and the title had to wait, so this is the perfect pressure test, because he wants to prove it.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The question everywhere is how much of Antonelli's success is down to his ability, and the answer is a lot, a very lot.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Future rules talk is also buzzing, with simpler cheaper hybrid V8s proposed, but right now all eyes are on this weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Let us start with the top three, and I am putting Kimi Antonelli first because he is season dominant and the title frontrunner, and the numbers say he is the one to beat.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: I agree. Mercedes pace is clear, and the illness is only a media day blip, not a warning sign for Sunday.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: His Mexico history is not his best, average sixth over one race, but form trumps history here, and he is flying.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: How do you beat the driver who is on the brink of a first world title, especially in a car that has been so strong?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Max Verstappen, second, because Red Bull pace is strong, and Mexico is his kind of track, and Max is always dangerous in a big race.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He has a win and two podiums over three Mexico races, averaging third point three, and that is a serious warning.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a real warning to Mercedes, because Max knows how to win there, and he loves the pressure of a big crowd.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Charles Leclerc, third, is the other Mexico specialist, and Ferrari have been in the mix when it matters.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Best Mexico history of the top three, average second point seven, best second, and three podiums over three races, and that history is hard to ignore.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ferrari has been consistent, and Charles has been in top three form recently, so he is not just a nostalgia pick.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I like Leclerc over Verstappen for third if Ferrari find the extra pace, but Max is too dangerous, and I cannot move him down.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the debate, but both are right there, and one small mistake could change the whole top three.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Deep cut time. Oliver Bearman is our tenth pick, and that is a low confidence gamble, but it is the kind we need.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Ha, Bearman is the wildcard, because Haas has circuit history and recent points, and he can make a lap count.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: If he gets the perfect lap, he can sneak into the points, and that is the kind of quirk we love in a preview.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Before the full list, remember that this weekend is about form, history, and a title that could finally be decided.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I love this field, because every pick has a reason, and the weekend can still surprise us.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: One last thought, the top three are close enough that one clean lap, one good start, or one small error can change everything.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Mexico City, title tension, and a lot of pace. This is the weekend to watch, and we are right here with you, with the title still in play.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Now here is the full top ten in order, first Kimi Antonelli, second Max Verstappen, third Charles Leclerc, fourth Lando Norris, fifth Lewis Hamilton, sixth George Russell, seventh Isack Hadjar, eighth Liam Lawson, ninth Pierre Gasly, tenth Oliver Bearman. We will see you at the race.
